I'm always open to hearing specific counterarguments—especially if those researchers shared compelling points with you!—but simply knowing that your circle agrees it's a net positive isn't enough to change my mind. Consensus in a particular group doesn't automatically make a view right, and truth isn't really a numbers game.

Besides, while it might be rare in your immediate circle, skepticism about social media's net impact is hardly a fringe stance globally. Plenty of sociologists, psychologists, and even former tech executives who built these platforms argue that the business model of monetizing human attention has caused deep structural harm—from fueling teen mental health crises to fracturing shared reality and eroding democratic discourse. 

I don't deny the positives, like helping marginalized people find community, organizing grassroots movements, or keeping long-distance friends connected. Those matter. Give me the actual arguments your friends and colleagues made, though! What makes them—and maybe you—feel those benefits outweigh the systemic downsides?
